A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DLLM-MEM and 3DMEM-BENCH work. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-H are readable and matchable; v2 principally adds a checklist and disclosures.

before.justification: v1 reports original embodied-task, question-answering and captioning results in Table 2, memory-initialization ablations in Table 3, and qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 2-3 and the qualitative demonstrations, including those in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same LLaVA-3D foundation, working and episodic memories, attention-based fusion, and memory-update procedure. The training objective and proposed components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HM3D/Objaverse-based benchmark, in-domain and in-the-wild embodied tasks, five EQA categories, and captioning tasks. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2a-2b retain identical comparator membership: finetuned 3D-LLM, Everything in Context, Most Recent Memory, Retrieval-Augmented Memory, and the three 3D-Mem variants using GPT4-o, Gemini-2.5-Flash and Gemini-2.5-Pro.

E3.justification: The difficulty settings, data splits, training budgets, context lengths and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendix G's baseline adaptations, truncation procedure and training epochs already appear in v1; their changed placement does not indicate revised experiments.

E4.justification: Both retain the same query-initialization ablation comparing working memory, recent episodic memory and learnable zero parameters in Table 3. The qualitative examples in Figures 4 and 6 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 explicitly states in checklist item 7 that computational expense prevented repeated experiments and error-bar calculation. This adds information about statistical reporting, without adding uncertainty estimates or establishing a change in runs performed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2-3 and the qualitative findings are retained. For example, average embodied-task success remains 37.6% in-domain and 32.1% in-the-wild for 3DLLM-MEM; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The representation definitions and memory-fusion equation (1) are unchanged. Neither version contains new theorems or proofs; the added checklist merely confirms their absence.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark and memory-model contributions, generalization claims, and claimed 16.5% advantage on in-the-wild embodied tasks.

C2.justification: Checklist item 7 newly acknowledges the computational constraint preventing repeated experiments and uncertainty estimates. Existing result interpretations, the limitation to high-level simulator policies in Section 6, and the broader-impact discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The checklist adds a future code/data release commitment, statements about supplementary sample code, data and documentation, release-use guidelines, and clarification that authors performed human validation. These are added disclosures; Appendices D and G retain the same implementation details, and actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited research, related-work discussion and novelty positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic differences concern citation-page references following document reflow.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments, funding and conflict-of-interest disclosures, and a NeurIPS checklist before Appendix A. The publication footer changes from Preprint to NeurIPS 2025, while the scientific prose and original section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: All six figures and seven tables retain their content and designs. The additions reflow references and appendices, changing prompt-table placement; notably, Tables 6 and 7 share a page in v2 instead of appearing on separate pages.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency about funding, conflicts, absent repeated runs and planned resource release. However, checklist item 16 says LLMs were used only for grammar, conflicting with the retained Gemini-based data generation and evaluation described in Section 2 and Appendix E. With the scientific content unchanged, these limited disclosure benefits and the new inconsistency leave the net quality direction uncertain.
